# How long it takes

Measured against a public, carousel-heavy account: **166 seconds for 5 posts -
about 33 seconds per post**, producing 45 files and 57 MB.

| Posts | Rough time |
| --- | --- |
| 5 | ~3 minutes |
| 20 | ~10 minutes |
| **45** | **~25 minutes** |
| 100 | ~55 minutes |

Most of that is deliberate waiting, not transfer: 3-6 s between posts, 1-2 s
between carousel slides, and 3 s on each video slide so the browser actually
requests the file. A profile of single photos runs far quicker than one full
of 16-slide carousels, so treat these as a middle estimate rather than a
promise.

Video-heavy private accounts are considerably slower than the public account
measured above - roughly **100-200 s per post** rather than 33 s, because each
video slide waits for playback to start and then downloads the file.

## Ways to spend less time

| | Time |
| --- | --- |
| [`scan`](commands.qmd#scan), which downloads nothing | **~3 s a post**, against 30 for archiving |
| [`--resume`](options.qmd) over a finished archive of 39 posts | **29 s**, against 14 minutes |
| [`fill-videos`](commands.qmd#fill-videos) for 15 videos across 6 posts | **131 s**, against about 14 minutes |

`--resume` skips posts the index shows are already complete, instead of
visiting each one to discover there is nothing to do. A post counts as
complete when the index holds rows for it and, if you asked for videos, none
of them is still a placeholder.

`--force` does the opposite: it ignores the index and fetches everything
again, which is what you want after changing *what* gets saved.

## Watching it run

A status line is printed after every post:

```text
  [######..................]  26.7%  12/45 posts | 148 files | 09:12 elapsed | ~25:18 left
```

Leave it running. Re-running is cheap - everything already in the index is
skipped - so an interrupted run picks up where it left off.
